title: Expose authoritative block and assist context through live play, replay and recovery
body:
# Feature: Expose authoritative block and assist context through live play, replay and recovery

## Abstract
Expose counted assist identities, projected blocking squares, and committed block context without changing gameplay.

## Objective
Expose counted assist identities, projected blocking squares, and committed block context without changing gameplay.

## Context / Existing Behavior
Existing block previews expose dice without contributor identities, and block context is unclear during opponent die selection. The user approved the C2 visual study after reviewing three coordinated designs and its refinements.

Browser MUTP only. Ordinary blocks, blitz blocks, repeated blocks (including Frenzy), and Multiple Block are included. Special attacks replacing normal block resolution and Java desktop changes are excluded. Private previews begin on explicit target selection; committed context is shared with both coaches and spectators. Recompute proposals before the roll, freeze contributing assists after the roll, and clear a block's markers when its target moves, the block finishes, or the proposal is cancelled. Multiple Block keeps both target-direction markers but only the current block's assists. Replay shows committed contexts only; recovery restores them. No backward compatibility for existing games is required. Server presentation metadata is allowed, but mechanics, dice, eligibility and sequence must not change.

## In Scope
- Native counted assist contributors, adjacent previews and route-endpoint blitz previews.
- Committed per-block lifecycle context, including repeated/Multiple Block and both coach/spectator views.
- Persistence, frozen replay snapshots, strict payload validation, and focused server tests.

## Out of Scope
- Gameplay/rules/sequence changes, special replacement attacks, Java desktop UI, backward compatibility, publishing or deployment.

## Functional Requirements
- Reuse the existing native assist eligibility calculation; do not duplicate rules in the browser.
- Include attacker/target identity and squares, counted offensive/defensive contributor identities and squares, and target-specific Multiple Block context.
- Refresh before rolling, freeze contributors after rolling, and clear on target movement or completion.
- Persist context at native state/replay/recovery boundaries and never expose private proposals.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Expose counted assist identities, projected blocking squares, and committed block context without changing gameplay.
- Approved cross-role visibility, lifecycle clearing, Multiple Block separation, replay and recovery behavior are covered by appropriate tests.
- Validation evidence and self-review results are recorded with the local design mirror.

## Constraints
- New implementation branch from current main; preserve approved mockup artifacts and unrelated working-tree changes.
- Follow repository Java 8/service/import/ruleset conventions and existing browser architecture.
- Preserve MUTP colors, type, themes and support on Android/Windows/Linux browsers.
- Do not stage, commit, push, create a PR, merge or deploy without further authorization.

## Implementation Guidance
Browser MUTP only. Ordinary blocks, blitz blocks, repeated blocks (including Frenzy), and Multiple Block are included. Special attacks replacing normal block resolution and Java desktop changes are excluded. Private previews begin on explicit target selection; committed context is shared with both coaches and spectators. Recompute proposals before the roll, freeze contributing assists after the roll, and clear a block's markers when its target moves, the block finishes, or the proposal is cancelled. Multiple Block keeps both target-direction markers but only the current block's assists. Replay shows committed contexts only; recovery restores them. No backward compatibility for existing games is required. Server presentation metadata is allowed, but mechanics, dice, eligibility and sequence must not change.

Approved visual contract: Use approved C2 from browser-client/prototypes/block-assists: ivory compact block arrow with original impact burst; gold offensive circle (radius .1725 pitch squares); cyan defensive diamond (half-diagonal .21) rotated so its forward vertex joins the shaft; defensive chevron flush with its endpoint bar. Shafts start at origin boundaries with no segment inside symbols. Assists render above threats and below sprites. Two glowing chasers traverse opposite origin sides, converge at the shaft, and travel down it. Block glow starts at arrow base, then traverses opposite ends of the unchanged impact shape, meeting with a brighter flare. Preserve reduced motion and MUTP themes.

Local design mirror: docs/specs/block-assist-visibility.md. Outcome: docs/specs/block-assist-visibility-outcome.md.

## Validation
Native/server tests for ordinary, Guard/cancelled/ineligible assists, route endpoint changes, uphill die ownership, repeated and Multiple Block targets, clearing, deterministic replay and recovery; relevant Maven build.

## Completion Notes
Run required checks, diagnose failures, and report exact results. Keep this issue open pending delivery review; implementation and validation alone do not authorize publication.
